comments.text: I’m thinking how they use the water from the ocean because is salt water for the agriculture?

replies.author: @ImpossibleTravel38
replies.text:
Haha, got you! Simply put, you can't pour ocean water directly onto normal crops—the salt will totally kill them.But here is how people actually make it work:
Desalination: They pass ocean water through massive filters to strip out the salt and turn it into fresh water. Places like Israel do this a lot.

Seawater Greenhouses: They pump ocean water into special greenhouses. The sun evaporates the water, leaves the salt behind, and creates fresh water vapor that condenses to water the plants.

Special Crops: Scientists are breeding "salt-loving" plants (like certain types of rice, seaweed, or kale) that can actually drink brackish or salty water without dying.So yeah, it takes some serious tech, but it’s totally a thing!
